events.location: Main Stage, LeBauer Park, Downtown Greensboro
events.description:
HEADLINER ANNOUNCEMENT

He came to Greensboro Pride in 2025 and left a mark. Now he’s coming back.

RYAN CASSATA

Singer-songwriter. Actor. Activist. Transgender motivational speaker. Signed to Kill Rock Stars. Over 800 performances worldwide. Eight albums. The first openly trans performer at the Vans Warped Tour.

Billboard called him “a true force in the industry.” His music video “Daughter” has over 2.5 million views on YouTube and 3.5 million streams on Spotify.

Ryan has been fighting for transgender liberation since he was 13. Larry King Live at 15. Harvard. The U.S. Capitol. The White House. The inaugural Harvey Milk Memorial Award from Harvey Milk’s own alma mater. The youngest keynote speaker in the history of the Philadelphia Trans Health Conference.

He’s back on our Main Stage and we could not be more proud.

Saturday, September 12, 2026 Main Stage | LeBauer Park | Downtown Greensboro

More headliners to come.… 👀

events.title: 🌈 Purina Chow at Greensboro Pride
events.location: Main Stage, LeBauer Park, Downtown Greensboro
events.description:
HEADLINER ANNOUNCEMENT

Greensboro, this one is an absolute LEGEND.

PURINA CHOW

Over 40 YEARS of entertaining audiences. A legendary comedy drag queen. A long-term HIV/AIDS survivor. An activist who has spent DECADES raising funds for HIV/AIDS care and local community support right here in North Carolina.

Purina Chow is colorful, hilarious, and unapologetically herself, a comedy queen through and through. And she carries something powerful with her every time she takes the stage: her memorial pearl necklaces. Each pearl represents a soul lost to HIV/AIDS, friends, idols, and those who died silently with no one to remember them. It is one of the most moving tributes in our community.

She is a living reminder of grace, strength, and courage, and she’s bringing all of it to our Main Stage.

Saturday, September 12, 2026
Main Stage | LeBauer Park | Downtown Greensboro

More headliners still to come… 👀

#GreensboroPride #IMPAQTGSO #pride🌈 #Greensboro

events.title: 🎨 GPS Student Residency Program: Studio Practices
events.description:
MEET MACY ✨ Current Artist in Residence, as part of the GPS Student Residency Program | Summer Studios: Arts on Site! ✨

About Macy macyjart 
Macy James (BFA Sculpture & Ceramics) will explore various materials that she has yet to try, though has long wanted to. Within this residency, Macy plans to work with more accessible material specifically, in addition to those she is accustomed to, like found and second-hand goods sourced from local places - materials that do not require large shops or expensive tools. Another material interest is found wood, like driftwood, to experiment with wood carving or wood burning alongside bead and wire sculptures, which she presently has no experience working with. The hope is that this will help her develop a healthy habit of creating art with widely accessible materials and make her an overall more multifaceted artist.

About the Student Residency Program:
Designed to support UNCG undergraduate student artists (BA + BFA) striving to develop, adapt, and/or reinvent their creative process and to promote artistic growth and development, artists are afforded two-weeks of uninterrupted research and development, coupled with financial support and public presentational platforms to share their creative work.

events.title: 🎨 GPS Student Residency Program: Summer Studios at Arts on Site
events.description:
MEET ELISSA ✨ Current Artist in Residence, as part of the GPS Student Residency Program | Summer Studios: Arts on Site! ✨

About Elissa elissa.artist 
Elissa Ukhueligbe (BFA Painting) plans to expand their practice through video and sound. The proposed idea is to animate photos into video and projections, mimicking a low “frames per second.” Using film, photos, drawings, or smaller paintings, they would mix video/sound with traditional art. Elissa is a multi-media artist that uses portraits of women to communicate complex ideas about femininity, self-expression, and gendered norms. They are interested in psychological exploration; how the media we consume affects us internally and externally.

events.title: 🎨 Homebody MFA Thesis Exhibition
events.description:
Thank you to everyone who joined us for the reception of Homebody by Kathryn Hood!🥂

The exhibition is still open until 5pm — don’t miss out on experiencing Homebody

************************
NOW OPEN @ GPS
Homebody

MFA Thesis Exhibition
by Kathryn Hood

Exhibition: April 28 - May 2, 2026
Reception: Friday, May 1st, 6-8p

Gallery Open Hours:
Tuesday - Friday 12-5p
Saturday, 2-5p

Homebody is an exhibition of collages and sculptures in which Kathryn Hood carves her perceptions of tense muscles into paper and upholstery foam. She embraces the body-mind connection, an essential tool for self-understanding, as she houses ungrounded avatars within handmade paper and muscular furnishings outside of formal traditions. Hood composes the interior feelings of ideas & emotions with the exterior feeling of tension. This duality of perception reflects the disparate nature of themes explored, such as femininity, domesticity, and the performance of identity.

Homebody is the residence of textured perceptions. This space is an act of resensitization.

Learn more by clicking “Happening Now” in the Linktree above in our profile

events.description:
Our LAST MFA Thesis Exhibition of the semester ✨ Join us in welcoming, Kathryn Hood, as we conclude “thesis season” at GPS! Here’s a look at install from yesterday, up for this week only, so come by and pop see for yourself!

Join us on Friday, May 1st 6-8p for a celebratory reception! 🥂

************************
NOW OPEN @ GPS
Homebody

MFA Thesis Exhibition
by Kathryn Hood

Exhibition: April 28 - May 2, 2026
Reception: Friday, May 1st, 6-8p

Gallery Open Hours: 
Tuesday - Friday 12-5p
Saturday, 2-5p

Homebody is an exhibition of collages and sculptures in which Kathryn Hood carves her perceptions of tense muscles into paper and upholstery foam. She embraces the body-mind connection, an essential tool for self-understanding, as she houses ungrounded avatars within handmade paper and muscular furnishings outside of formal traditions. Hood composes the interior feelings of ideas & emotions with the exterior feeling of tension. This duality of perception reflects the disparate nature of themes explored, such as femininity, domesticity, and the performance of identity.

Homebody is the residence of textured perceptions. This space is an act of resensitization.

NOW OPEN @ GPS
Garden of Corporeal Fantasy
MFA Thesis Exhibition
by Victoria Mercado-Lues

Exhibition: April 21 - 25, 2026
Reception: Friday, April 24th, 6-8p

Gallery Open Hours:
Tuesday - Friday 12-5p
Saturday, 2-5p

Brightly saturated and fantastical, Garden of Corporeal Fantasy explores the meeting of nature and flesh in oil paintings and ceramics. With invented creatures and visceral biological imagery, the works reframe the gaze towards the bodily through a lens of wonder — a less punitive lens than the centuries-long and still recurring traditions of bodies as commodified, objectified, or sinful.

This exhibition addresses our discomfort surrounding the body by combining it with the godly imposing presence of the landscape, like waterfalls and billowing clouds. In this combination, the work is imbued with a devotional, almost sacred quality, borrowing visuals of the holy and filling it with the biological. The sticky, hairy, fleshy becomes something worth staring at with open fascination, the same way we are in awe of exotic plants, or deep-sea creatures, illuminating the sublime inherent in the corporeal.

events.title: 🎨 Death Circle
events.description:
𝔇𝔢𝔞𝔱𝔥 ℭ𝔦𝔯𝔠𝔩𝔢, 𝔱𝔬𝔡𝔞𝔶 𝔣𝔯𝔬𝔪 5 𝔱𝔬 7 𝔓𝔐 

So many of us are carrying a lot right now. Personal losses, collective grief, the ache of what is happening in the world, and the grief we feel for our more-than-human kin and planet. We were never meant to carry any of this alone. What does it mean to live and die consciously? This circle is an offering to unburden ourselves in shared community and, in doing so, perhaps find more spaciousness and imaginative possibilities. 

Together we will co-create a sacred space to remember that these tender conversations about death, grief, cycles of change, and all of our connections in this web of existence once lived at the center of our communities. They are an integral part of our collective wellbeing. 

Death Circle is not a therapeutic setting or a grief support group, but an invitation to be present with one another as we explore these topics and reconnect more deeply with ourselves, each other, and the world around us. We welcome your curiosities, stories, questions, as well as your silence. There is no pressure to speak. All of it belongs 🖤

Our hope is that this offering fosters clarity, nurtures care, and deepens our relational intimacy. 

Death Circle will be held on the last Sunday of every month, from 5-7pm. We’ll have coffee and donuts, but feel free to bring your own snacks or any comfort items that support you.

We look forward to seeing you there — 
Joshua & Bri

events.title: 🎨 advance_base & moontypo with likewindowpanes
events.description:
advance_base & moontypo are coming back to Greensboro with local support from likewindowpanes on Wednesday, February 25th 👾🎶🎹

Doors at 7pm and music at 8pm // $12 suggested 

This is going to be a really sweet show. We’re super thrilled to have these folks back in Greensboro. If you missed Advance Base for his winter tour in 2024 or Moontype last summer, this is your chance to see them both with Greensboro’s own, Panes. 

Advance Base is the melancholic soft rock recording project of Chicago, IL singer/songwriter Owen Ashworth (formerly of Casiotone for the Painfully Alone). Using a two-handed arsenal of electric piano, Omnichord, samplers, effect pedals & drum machines, Ashworth builds minimalist, heavy-hearted, nostalgia-obsessed ballads around his conversational baritone. The warm, electronic sound of Advance Base has been described as “lo-fi,” “depressed” & “weirdly uplifting.” Advance Base released Horrible Occurrences in 2024.

Moontype is songwriter Margaret McCarthy’s dreamworld come to life. Based in Chicago, Illinois, the band features Emerson Hunton on drums, and Joe Suihkonen and Andrew Clinkman on guitar. Quiet emotions that McCarthy explores with her bass become, with the band, as large and as musically complex as a mood itself: cathartic, angsty, and unmet. Moontype released their debut album, Bodies of Water, in 2021 to critical acclaim.

panes is minimal introspective music with an engaging, dreamy listlessness. ever careening toward some kind of undiscovered self epiphany.

Flyer by: likewindowpanes

This project is 100% improv—noisy ambient colliding with avant jazz. brian.s.haran likewindowpanes _tyler.monroe_ 

𝙇𝙪𝙠𝙚 𝙎𝙘𝙝𝙣𝙚𝙞𝙙𝙚𝙧 is a Nashville based pedal steel guitarist who has worked with a variety of artists including Margo Price, Orville Peck, S.G. Goodman, William Tyler, and Futurebirds. His debut solo album of ambient New Age music created entirely on pedal steel, ‘Altar of Harmony,’ was released by Third Man Records in 2020. His new EP ‘For Dancing In Quiet Light’ is out now via Leaving Records. lukefromnashville 

𝙎𝙖𝙖𝙥𝙖𝙩𝙤 is the music project of upstate New York–based sound artist Brendan Principato, who weaves manipulated field recordings with lush electronic soundscapes exploring ecology and music. He has held residencies with the National and Alaska State Park Services, including 2023 near Juneau and 2022 on Fire Island. His recordings have been named Best Ambient on Bandcamp, and his live performances include collaborations with Laraaji, Don Slepian, Patricia Wolf, and Green-House. saapato

events.title: 🎨 Death Circle
events.description:
𝔇𝔢𝔞𝔱𝔥 ℭ𝔦𝔯𝔠𝔩𝔢, 𝔱𝔬𝔡𝔞𝔶 𝔣𝔯𝔬𝔪 5 𝔱𝔬 7 𝔓𝔐 

So many of us are carrying a lot right now. Personal losses, collective grief, the ache of what is happening in the world, and the grief we feel for our more-than-human kin and planet. We were never meant to carry any of this alone. What does it mean to live and die consciously? This circle is an offering to unburden ourselves in shared community and, in doing so, perhaps find more spaciousness and imaginative possibilities. 

Together we will co-create a sacred space to remember that these tender conversations about death, grief, cycles of change, and all of our connections in this web of existence once lived at the center of our communities. They are an integral part of our collective wellbeing. 

Death Circle is not a therapeutic setting or a grief support group, but an invitation to be present with one another as we explore these topics and reconnect more deeply with ourselves, each other, and the world around us. We welcome your curiosities, stories, questions, as well as your silence. There is no pressure to speak. All of it belongs 🖤

Our hope is that this offering fosters clarity, nurtures care, and deepens our relational intimacy. 

Death Circle will be held on the last Sunday of every month, from 5-7pm. We’ll have coffee and donuts, but feel free to bring your own snacks or any comfort items that support you.

We look forward to seeing you there — 
Joshua & Bri

events.title: 🎨 DAGGERTEETH
events.description:
DAGGERTEETH TOMORROW TOMORROW TOMORROW.
.
ARE Y'ALL PUMPED CUZ WE CAN'T WAIT TO OPEN OUR DOORS TO YOU TOMORROW!
.
Teeth don't lie. They bite, they tear, they mark what they touch.

Traditional printmaking techniques meet zine culture's raw urgency. Punk aesthetics slash through the white cube aesthetic and screams to be heard.

Every piece here carries evidence of hands—ink rolled, paper pressed, screens burned, images carved. The tactility of making things physical in a digital age. These works don't apologize for their rough edges. They weaponize them.

DAGGERTEETH celebrates artists who create outside institutional approval, distribution systems built on photocopiers and kitchen tables, aesthetics born from necessity and defiance. The underground made visible.

Sharp work for sharp teeth.

**February 21, 2026 | 5PM-8PM**

Irving Park Art & Frame

2800 Lawndale Dr. Ste 107, Greensboro, NC

events.title: 🎵 Treee City
events.description:
This Saturday the 15th!
9pm - 2am

Deeply embedded in North Carolina’s thriving electronic music scene, Treee City is a Durham-based DJ and producer whose dynamic presence has left an indelible mark on dance floors and festivals alike. As a founding member of Durham’s iconic Party Illegal (https://partyillegal.com/) soundsystem, he’s helped cultivate a vibrant underground culture. He has releases on Raund Haus and Maison Fauna have showcased his talent for crafting irresistible grooves.
Treee City’s performances are a testament to his versatility and energy, with appearances at premier festivals like Moogfest, Hopscotch, and Slingshot. He’s shared stages with the likes of Sylvan Esso (https://www.sylvanesso.com/), Steve Aoki (https://steveaoki.com/), Washed Out (https://www.facebook.com/washed.out/), and Daedelus (https://www.facebook.com/Daedelusmusic/), solidifying his reputation as a powerhouse performer. His debut album, “Good Job (https://raundhaus.bandcamp.com/album/good-job)“, released last November on Raund Haus Records, was hailed as “something special…filled with dance-floor heaters” (Indy Week (https://indyweek.com/)).
Beyond the studio and stage, Treee City continues to build community through music. He organizes “Blends With Friends“, a biweekly DJ open decks and music meetup at The Pinhook (https://thepinhook.com/), and “Moodboard“, a monthly club night at Rubies (httpshttps://rubiesnc.com/) in collaboration with Mamis and the Papis (https://www.facebook.com/mamisandthepapis/).
Whether he’s curating a crowd or dropping his signature sound, Treee City is a force that pushes boundaries and elevates the electronic scene in North Carolina and beyond.

The ‘Boro Sessions proudly presents “Daniel Ayers, Sounds of North
Carolina” a seated, listening room concert on Sunday afternoon, August 16,
2:00-4:00pm / doors open at 1:00pm (location: 221 Summit Ave,
Greensboro, NC, the Flat Iron). Tickets are $20 plus taxes and fees in
advance/ $25 plus taxes and fees day of show. 

A tenth-generation North Carolinian, Daniel draws inspiration from NC
songwriting greats like Bruce Piephoff and David Childers, absorbing the
stories, sounds, and soul of the Old North State. As co-host of The
Hometown Holler podcast, Daniel has built a devoted following by
celebrating all things North Carolina, connecting audiences across the state
and far beyond its borders. What began as a hobby to give voice to the
untold stories of local community issues has transformed into a podcast with
more than 60 guests and millions of views. Guests have included Josh Stein,
Pat McCrory, Roy Cooper, Anita Earls, and numerous journalists. Daniel
studied history at Roanoke College and taught both history and civics classes
when he returned to North Carolina.
Whether he’s strumming an original tune or singing an old-time murder
ballad, Daniel Ayers sounds like home!!
The venue sells beer, wine, spirits, and sodas. FREE parking: available in
the lot across the street, in the gravel lot across the street from the main
lot, as well as behind the Greensboro Historical Museum.

events.title: 🎵 Irata
events.description:
Tonight, August the 8th!
Doors at 7pm
Show at 8pm

Since its 2007 genesis at the hands of founding members Jon Case and Jason Ward, Irata has mutated relentlessly. Through four previous records, the band has never sat idly in any specific style, while maintaining a signature mesmerizing, grinding pulse between bass and drums that permeates an enigmatic vision of heavy rock. After releasing ‘Tower’ in 2019 as a four-piece, Irata is once again a trio, and continues to push forward into new sonic territories.

On ‘Human,’ the band is building on the structures that have created some of its enduring favorites — namely, thundering bass riffs, hypnotic drums, and grandiose choruses. They do not sacrifice expression for refinement, but manage to have it both ways. Their progression is evident in the patience with which “Altar” leads off, a melodic confidence that overarches the eight included songs, and the atmospheres in pieces like “Slipped” (see “pulse…” above) and the expansive finale “Daystar,” but none of ‘Human’ is so overblown as to give up its organically dynamic nature.

And perhaps in an era marked by the advent of machine-made art, ‘Human’ can be as much a statement of purpose as a declaration of self. In any case, with this collection of songs, Irata’s focus on vocal melody and intricate riffing distinguish them from a crowded underground sphere. The record moves as two sides of one image, opening with reflections of a final chapter, and closing with reflections of a new beginning through transformation; a story being told as it’s lived. What could be more human than that?

‘Human’ was recorded with longtime friends Hunter Allen and Adam Joyce of The Bronzed Chorus at Amplified Acres in Liberty, NC, and mixed by J. Robbins at The Magpie Cage in Baltimore, MD.

events.title: 🎵 Hiroya Tsukamoto Performance
events.description:
Today, Saturday the 8th!
Doors at 2:30pm
Show at 3pm

Experience the spellbinding artistry of Hiroya Tsukamoto / a master of fingerstyle guitar and evocative storytelling that transcends cultural boundaries. 
 
Praised by Acoustic Guitar Magazine for his “delicate, fluid, and beautifully details” style, Hiroya’s music weaves intricate melodies with poetic narratives, creating an unforgettable, soul-stirring performance.

Hiroya Tsukamoto is a Japanese-born fingerstyle guitarist who moved to the United States in 2000 to attend the Berklee College of Music. Needless to say, he’s not only a dizzyingly agile fingerpicker, but a soulful and transcendent performer, with compositions that combine instrumental guitar work with lyrical performance and spoken stories from his life. 

Tsukamoto has been recognized for his talents on stages such as at Blue Note in New York City, NHK Television,  International Storytelling Center and United Nations, and by scoring second place at the International Fingerstyle Guitar Championship both in 2018 and 2022.

events.title: 🎵 Desmond Myers & Aaron Rizzo
events.description:
Tonight, Wednesday the 5th!
Doors at 7pm
Show at 8pm

Desmond Myers is an Atlanta-based singer-songwriter and producer. His music is bolstered by a smooth understated tenor voice, moody colorful arrangements with earnest lyrics. Whether behind a guitar or a synthesizer, his music is full of clever restraint, energy and mood. 

After spending a decade living in France he was exposed to the indie-funk/disco scene and it left an unmistakable mark on his music. His album Shadowdancer (recorded in France) reflects this sound and it’s breakout single “Playing with Fire” has been streamed over 4 million times.

 In summer 2026, he’s releasing his third album “Superdomestic” with the single “Balloon” along with dates along the east coast. 

Aaron Rizzo is an independent rock artist from Rochester, New York whose original work has fostered acclaim from listeners all over the globe. His music has appeared on television shows such as Shameless, Black-Ish and in a T-Mobile ad. In the spring of 2025, Rizzo appeared on NBC’s hit television show The Voice, where he worked closely with Canadian singer Michael Bublé.

A guitar player by nature and a singer by trade, Aaron Rizzo writes, records and produces music for himself and others in Atlanta, Georgia where he is based. It’s here that he has sharped his toolset, making him a Swiss Army knife of a musician that can thrive in just about any environment.

To date, Rizzo has recorded four full-length solo albums that eloquently showcase his diversity as an original artist. Each one of his records explores a different corner of his ability, all with two common denominators — prolific songwriting and articulate guitar work. In addition to his own catalog, he has recorded and produced countless songs for other artists. He has composed original scores for two short films, one of which that went on to win Best Score at the Sick ’N Wrong Film Festival.

events.title: 🤝 Geodes, Gemstones, and Geology program
events.description:
Explore a variety of rocks and minerals at the Geodes, Gemstones, and Geology program!

We'll learn about the science and beauty of rocks, create some geode art, and take home a gemstone. This program is for children and families.

📍 Hemphill Branch
📅 Tuesday, August 4
⏰ 2:30 - 3:30 pm

Do you know what the difference is between a rock and a mineral? 💎
According to the British Geological Survey, a mineral is a naturally occurring substance with distinctive chemical and physical properties, composition and atomic structure. Rocks are generally made up of two of more minerals, mixed up through geological processes.

events.title: 🤝 Special Meeting: Borders are prisons and prisons are borders
events.description:
Greensboro Revolutionary Socialists would like to invite you to join us this Monday, February 10 at 7pm at 1333 Grove St for a special meeting, featuring a talk by organizer Kristen Godfrey on their article, "Borders are prisons and prisons are borders" with a discussion to follow.

*

"The way working-class people experience borders all over the world is tied to the theft of land and surplus value. Settler-colonialism’s life source is criminality and illegality, which is why we must be anti-capitalist abolitionists, developing a critical analysis of how imperialists’ tactics work to divide us."

*

Tell us how this new context impacts you. Let's think about how we can resist together.
 Group of revolutionary socialists in Greensboro, NC and members of Tempest Collective @tempest_mag

events.title: 🎵 Sunday Night Birthday Finale
events.description:
Our Sunday night birthday finale headed by ISH K

ISH K is a Melbourne-based electronic artist known for his immersive blend of psytrance and progressive psychedelic music. With releases on PsyFeature, Odiva Records, Synk87 and Spin Twist Records, his sound combines driving basslines, hypnotic grooves and intricate psychedelic sound design.
A regular on Australia’s festival circuit, ISH K has performed at Esoteric Festival, Rabbits Eat Lettuce, Blossom Festival, Rainbow Spirit, Bohemian Beatfreaks, Dangerous Goods XXL and AURA. Internationally, he’s taken his sound to Universo Paralello in Brazil and NYX Festival in Mexico, delivering powerful, emotional dancefloor journeys to psychedelic communities around the world.

events.title: 🤝 Downtown Neighborhood Association First Meeting
events.location: The Crown at the Carolina Theatre
events.description:
CALLING ALL DOWNTOWN RESIDENTS! 🗣️🌃

Over the past four months, DGI staff have been meeting with downtown residents, property managers, City Council members, and other downtown management nonprofits to help develop the new Downtown Neighborhood Association. 
 
Our first meeting is August 12th at 5:30 p.m. at The Crown at the Carolina Theatre, where we’ll hear directly from downtown residents about what they want to see from the association and what matters most to them as people who live downtown.

The Downtown Neighborhood Association is resident-focused and designed specifically to give downtown residents a space to connect, share their experiences, raise concerns, and help shape the future of downtown living.

If you live downtown, we want to hear from you. Come be part of the conversation and help shape what this new association can become.

events.title: 🌈 Miss Gay North Carolina America Pageant
events.description:
👑 Tonight, One More of Our Queens Becomes a “Forever”! 👑
Tonight, our very own Malayia Chanel Iman (malayiachaneliman)  takes the stage to crown her successor as Miss Gay North Carolina America!

💖 Chemistry Nightclub could not be prouder of Malayia and the incredible reign she has had over the past year. Your grace, talent, dedication, and representation have made us so proud to call you one of our own. We love you, and hope you have an absolutely amazing step-down! 👑

🌟 To all of tonight's contestants:
We wish each and every one of you an incredible pageant experience! While only one contestant will take home the crown tonight, every one of you has already shown the talent, drive, heart, and determination it takes to wear this title.  And honestly... we can't pick just one to cheer for! So many of you are part of the Chemistry family. Just know that Chemistry is incredibly proud to continue working with so many and would be honored to have you represent this title!

👑 CHEMISTRY'S INCREDIBLE LEGACY
We have to take a moment to recognize the remarkable representation our house cast has brought to this pageant! Chemistry Nightclub's house cast divas have won the last FIVE out of SIX competitions! If you count our extended drag family of performers, Of the past 15 reigns, 10 have brought it home! 
 👑  In no particular order: Vivian Vaughn, Paris Nicole Brooks-Bonet, Giselle Cassidy Carter, Saniya Chanel Iman, Aria Russo, Chloe Cassidy, Ariel Nicole Night Addams, Emory Starr, Kiara Mel, Jamie Monroe, Kirby Kolby, Devida, and now, Malayia Chanel Iman. 
We honestly couldn't be prouder of the level of talent and excellence our entertainers continue to bring to the stage. This legacy is something truly special, and we are honored to have watched these incredible performers represent Chemistry and Miss Gay NC America with such pride and excellence!

👑 Malayia, as you enjoy the rest of this very special day, please know that although previous commitments prevented us from being there with you tonight, the entire Chemistry Nightclub family is cheering for you from Greensboro! 📣
👑 Once a queen, always a queen, and forever a Chemistry Diva! 🌈
 Greensboro's LGBTQ+ nightclub

events.description:

events.title: 🌈 Pride Celebration: Family-Friendly Songs with Mr. Sam of Scuppernong's Saturday Get-Downs
events.description:
Are you ready to celebrate Pride?!? Pride in our gender identity, gender expression, and sexual orientation happens year-round, and it's also great to have opportunities to celebrate together!

Join us at the Pyrle Theater in downtown Greensboro for a day of celebration on Saturday, June 20. The fun kicks off in the afternoon with family-friendly songs led by Mr. Sam of Scuppernong's Saturday Get-Downs, followed by a pizza dance party for youth and teens. To close out the night, the 21+ crowd will be treated to performances by drag superstars Thigh Fieri, Franny Starlight, and Brenda the Drag Queen, with DJ SmoothE providing tunes throughout the evening.

The Pyrle will have food and drinks available to keep the fun going. Tickets will be available soon through the Pyrle, so stay tuned!

events.title: 🤝 Say Hey to Phoebe
events.description:
Announcing Phoebe Lawless (phoebe_lawless) as Fullsteam's new Director of Hospitality!

Many of you know Phoebe from her beloved Durham ventures over the years: Scratch, Baby Scratch, The Lakewood, and Snack Service. 

We are beyond thrilled to have Phoebe build and help execute our vision for what we're calling an "American South Public House" at fullsteamatc and its event space, Stoker Club.

Menu-wise, expect a blend of tavern classics (including the return of some Rigsbee favorites) and a ton of Southern sides. Plenty of vegan options, too...and not just "pick these sides that happen to be vegan."

We hope to open around Labor Day. (2026 😁)

For now, swing by this Friday from 4 to 7pm to say hey to Phoebe. Enjoy free hot dogs, beer samples, and tours of the new space! 
🌭 🍻 🎆

events.title: 🎨 Porsche Boxster S Raffle
events.description:
It's that time - Porsche raffle time! Now through November 1, enter for a chance to win a fully restored, custom-painted 2001 Porsche Boxster S.

As porsche.cary’s inaugural entry into the 2026 Porsche Restoration Challenge, a competition that seeks to return a vehicle as closely as possible to its original production specifications and condition, the team selected the car for this year’s raffle as a nod to the NCMA’s own art conservation team and upcoming Conservation Lab opening in 2027.

This raffle is offered by the North Carolina Museum of Art Foundation, Inc. All proceeds support NCMA programming. This raffle is in collaboration with Porsche Cary. Valued at $58,585.

events.title: 🎨 Knowing the West
events.description:
If you haven't visited the Knowing the West exhibition yet, today is the LAST DAY it will be on view at the NCMA!

The interplay of works by artists from various cultures, including white, Black, Hispanic, Asian American, and a wide range of distinct Native nations, compels reconsideration of what the West has meant and continues to mean to communities across generations.

We are open 10 am-5 pm. Tickets are available at the link in our bio.

events.title: 🎨 An Evening of Sacred Songs: Lala Tamar, Yacouba Sissoko, Zachi Asher, and Rich Stein
events.description:
Coming up on Sunday, August 16: Join Lala Tamar, African harpist and kora master Yacouba Sissoko, oud/guitarist Zachi Asher, and percussionist Rich Stein for a magical evening of sacred songs that bridge Jewish spiritual tradition with the sacred musical languages of West Africa and the Middle East.

Before the show, enjoy a pre-concert dinner at NCMA Café featuring signature favorites alongside special entrées inspired by the vibrant flavors of West Africa and the Middle East.

This program is an event of the Initiative for Jewish Art and Culture.

Click the link in our bio for tickets and dinner reservations.

Join us Saturday, August 8, for an engaging journey through the history and impact of Black artists in American music with Dom Flemons's "Bronze Buckaroo Film and Songster Show."

Through two acts, the show blends live music, film, and history to celebrate the legacy of Black cowboys and Black roots music.

Learn more and get your ticket at the link in our bio.

-------
Image: Courtesy of Dom Flemons

events.title: 🎨 Canopy of Love
events.description:
"Give and give, for it is never too little."
- African proverb

Artist thandiwe_muriu uses African proverbs to reveal another layer of her work in "Canopy of Love." This proverb, coupled with the subject’s strong pose and twisted hair, depicts women as trees that give relief, joy, wisdom, and life.

“A woman is not just an individual, but a special gathering place for her community," Muriu says.

As one of the newer additions to the People's Collection, this work has only been on display in West Building since May. Make sure to see it in person the next time you visit (if you haven't already) - it's really quite stunning.

--------
Pictured: Thandiwe Muriu, Canopy of Love, 2025, Jet ink print on FineArt RAG+ MATT 310g, 59 x 39 3/8 in., Purchased with funds from the North Carolina State Art Society (Robert F. Phifer Bequest)

events.title: 🎨 Bark Culture
events.description:
*SUPPORT ADDED* AUGUST 9 @ 7PM — On tour from Philadelphia, don’t miss the brilliance of Victor Veira-Branco’s BARK CULTURE now joined by openers HillHillHill (Chicago) and quaytheband (Durham). 

Bark Culture is a Philadelphia-based trio led by vibraphonist Victor Vieira-Branco, featuring Joey Sullivan on drums and John Moran on bass. The band is touring their new record The Giant is Awkward set for release on June 5th, 2026.

The Giant is Awkward is the second album by vibraphonist and composer Victor Vieira-Branco’s Bark Culture. The ensemble—featuring John Moran (double bass) and Joey Sullivan (drums)—is joined by pianist and composer Sam Yulsman for five pieces that mirror the prismatic nature of a sound Vieira-Branco has been tirelessly crafting with the group since 2021. With the addition of Yulsman, the group reveals, as Peter Margasak states, “a heightened sensitivity and grace, with increased harmonic splendor thanks to the added chordal voice. The record also marks the vibraphonist’s clear growth as a composer.”

The band’s 2024 debut, Warm Wisdom, received high praise, with New York Times jazz critic Hank Shteamer listing it among his top debuts of 2024, as well as landing a spot on Bandcamp’s Best of Jazz for September 2024. Since then, Vieira-Branco has joined Rob Mazurek’s Exploding Star Orchestra and the Chad Taylor Quintet, the former of which released the album Smokeshifter, featuring three pieces penned by the vibraphonist. The core trio of Bark Culture was also heavily involved in Rob Mazurek’s score for Kelly Reichardt’s 2025 film The Mastermind.

events.title: 🎨 5 Women - 5 Voices: In Form, Function, & Feminine Force
events.description:
Coming this August!
5 Women - 5 Voices: In Form, Function, & Feminine Force

August - September 2026
Opening Reception: Friday, August 14, 6-8:30pm
Featuring work by Irena Cepulyte, Theresa Arico, Alina Cochran, Tamara Buettner, and Susan Brubaker Knapp.

5 Women – 5 Voices is a vivid, tactile conversation—an exploration of 
the power of feminine force through material practice. It invites viewers to 
witness how the personal becomes universal, how utility becomes art, and how five distinct voices can rise together in harmony, strength, and purpose.

#art #5women #theartscenter

events.title: 🎨 Choir Camp (3rd-5th Grade)
events.description:
Instructor Feature!

Emily and Sierra have known each other for years, and both ended up teaching at ArtsCamp this summer! Emily, who specializes in vocals and music, has been teaching Choir Camp and Mix It Up with Sound, two 3rd-5th grade camps, and Sierra, who does visual art, has been teaching Sea Wonders, which is a K-2nd grade camp. If you'd like to see more of Sierra's work, you can follow her ceramics account, smiles_pottery. 

For Week 6, Emily will be teaching Choir Camp again! Parents of interested 3rd-5th graders can register their students at canvas.artscenterlive.org/classes. We hope to see you there!

events.title: 🤝 Unboxed: Art Beyond the Museum
events.location: NCMA Winston-Salem Downtown Art Space, 400 W. 4th St. Ste 130, Winston-Salem
events.description:
For nearly 70 years, ncma.winstonsalem has connected our community to contemporary art through inspiring exhibitions, educational programs, and cultural experiences. While the museum undergoes exciting capital improvements throughout 2026, it’s returning to where it all began—downtown Winston-Salem.

From July 16 through August 30, experience Unboxed: Art Beyond the Museum, the inaugural exhibition in NCMA Winston-Salem’s new downtown art space. Admission is free and open to the public.

Unboxed brings together artists who have contributed to the Museum’s Portable Gallery, an education initiative that places original works by North Carolina artists directly into schools across the state. Last year alone, the program connected more than 2,000 students with contemporary art.

Featuring artists at a variety of career stages, the exhibition explores themes of place, identity, and imagination through diverse subjects, materials, and artistic techniques that reflect the richness of North Carolina itself.

Whether you’re a longtime art lover or simply looking for something new to experience downtown, this is the perfect opportunity to step inside Winston-Salem’s newest creative space and celebrate the power of art to connect our community. 🎨✨

📍 400 W. 4th St. Ste 130

events.title: 🎵 An Evening with legendzeppelin
events.description:
Do NOT miss An Evening with legendzeppelin on October 8, 2026, in Gas Hill Drinking Room! Doors at 7 PM, show at 8 PM.

Tickets are on sale NOW at TheRamkat.com!

The ONLY band that can take you back to 1969 and give you the experience of SEEING Led Zeppelin right in front of you!

Don't miss this opportunity to see the only band with the equipment, attitude and musicianship of Led Zeppelin straight out of 1969.  Legend Zeppelin doesn't give you a playlist of hits, they demonstrate the same sonic assault of Led Zeppelin in their earliest tours of 1969.

Come see something no band has ever attempted; to journey through the career of Led Zeppelin from the beginnings of 1969 and progress to 1980 over a six year period of time.  Re-live the birth of your favorite songs into the set, the development of stage show and swagger as it all grows to an ultimate 1980 US tour that never was.

The world's first and only Bootleg Band - Legend Zeppelin. Welcome Back, 1969.

#legendzeppelin #bootleg #livemusic #ledzeppelin #ledzeppelinlive #1969 #gashilldrinkingroom #wsnc #supportlivemusic

events.title: 🎨 Sculpting Wire Flowers w/ Thaddeus
events.description:
🎨Come Make Art at ART CRUSH! Curated by the incredible Jaz there are two Art Educators ready to teach some free and exciting workshops during the event! 

Sculpting Wire Flowers w/ Thaddeus - 7:15-8:15PM
In this class you will learn to make a wire catchall that is stylized to look like a flower with a wooden base for support. During your time in this class you will gain first-hand experience utilizing wire shaping techniques, and additionally learn about my process for making more elaborate artwork. At the end of the class, you will leave with your very own Wire Flower Catchall unique to you.

Paint a Textured Earring w/ Bonnie - 8:30-9:30PM
Participants will choose a kit from a selection of several patterns; each kit contains two textured earring blanks and a pair of earwires. At the tables, they will use a brand of fast-drying metal paints to add color to their earrings, then use sanding tools (soft files and buﬀs) to remove the paint from the high points of the textures. They will then use pliers to attach the earrings to their earwires. I will demonstrate the techniques and help as necessary, but this is an activity that most people grasp very easily.

events.title: 🎨 ADWS Annual Meeting
events.description:
ART CRUSH is evolving, and we’re doing it with intention.

This year, we’re focusing on fewer, more thoughtfully planned events to create stronger experiences for artists, attendees, and the businesses that make the Arts District of Winston-Salem thrive.

Here’s what 2026 looks like:
🌈 May – Color the District
🏙️July – Winston-Salem Weekend
🎉 September – Hispanic Heritage Month
🛍️ November – Arts District Celebration

Each event is designed to feel meaningful, vibrant, and well-supported, with clearer themes, deeper engagement, and more space to do things really well.

What’s new for artists:
We’re introducing a $25 participation fee with 35 paid artist spots per event, plus 5 scholarship-funded spots for emerging artists. This helps sustain ART CRUSH while keeping access and opportunity at the center of what we do.

One more shift:
We’re moving away from annual memberships. Artists can now participate event by event: simple, flexible, and clear. (Full details coming to our website soon!)

Want the full story?
Join us for the ADWS Annual Meeting at chadschai 
📅 February 27 | ⏰ 6:00–7:30 PM

Come curious. Bring a friend who’s new to ART CRUSH. Stay for the conversation.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

events.title: 🎨 Acting Through Song Masterclass
events.description:
Fresh off their Junior Theatre Festival run, look what our rising sTArs have coming up next! ta.rising.stars 

✨ An unforgettable experience is coming to Winston-Salem! ✨

🎭 Tony Award-nominated Broadway star Kerry Butler is headlining an exclusive Acting Through Song Masterclass & Rising sTArs Broadway Cabaret hosted by Theatre Alliance Rising sTArs! 🌟

Kerry Butler has graced the Broadway stage originating roles in Beetlejuice, Mean Girls, Xanadu, Little Shop of Horrors, Catch Me If You Can, Hairspray, and so many more! 🌟 From Broadway to TV, she’s done it all! 📺

🎤 In this masterclass, eight performers will work one-on-one with Kerry and all attendees will receive invaluable tips on audition techniques, character development, and vocal performance. PLUS, there will be a Q&A! 🙌

🎶 After the class, join Kerry and local performers for a one-night-only cabaret event featuring show-stopping performances and behind-the-scenes stories from the Broadway world. 🎭✨

Want to sing on stage with Kerry? 🎤 Registration for the masterclass includes a ticket to the cabaret and the chance to perform LIVE! 🎶💥

📍 Location: Juxtaposition Studios, Winston-Salem, NC

events.description:
Don’t be an outsider looking in! Enjoy a matinee with us this Saturday!

“This Side of Crazy,” by Del Shores, is next in Theatre Alliance’s Beall Theatre! When three feuding sisters are summoned home by their popular gospel-music composing mother to perform one final musical concert, old tensions flare, and the outcome is anything but blessed and holy! Grab a front-row seat to the latest by the southern writer who brought us “Sordid Lives,” “Southern Baptist Sissies,” and “The Trials and Tribulations of a Trailer Trash Housewife!”

September 20 and 27 at 12 PM and 3 PM

Tickets: $15

Get them here: https://theatrealliance.ws/box-office/

Rated R for language, sexual content, mature subject matter

events.description:
Back to Baltimore tonight for “Hairspray!” Tonight’s forecast for rain presents an ideal opportunity to stay dry and enjoy an evening with a multi-Tony-Award-winning musical!

“Hairspray” bursts onto the Theatre Alliance stage in September!  If you aren’t familiar with this colorful confection of a show, you should be!  Follow 1960s teeny-bopper Tracy Turnblad and her friends and family as they navigate the fight for civil rights and everyone’s right to dance, because “You Can’t Stop The Beat!” Arguably featuring one of the best, high-energy scores in several decades, “Hairspray” is a show that celebrates the best in all of us!

Performing these dates at Winston-Salem Theatre Alliance’s Jamie Lawson Auditorium, 650 W Sixth Ave, Winston-Salem, NC:

September 12-13, 19-20 at 7:30 PM
September 14 and 21 at 2 PM
ADDED: September 26 and 27 at 7:30 PM

Free parking onsite!

Tickets: https://theatrealliance.ws/box-office/

events.title: 🌈 Get Shit Done Evening
events.description:
Some of the biggest barriers to survivor safety are finance related. While we do our best to put cash directly into survivors hands, in tandem, we thought it would be awesome to create a body doubling/coworking space where we can support each other in sifting through all the shit that goes into getting financial stable. And offer relevant financial resources as we find them! That’s why we host our “Get Shit Done” evenings. They will occur the 1st & 3rd Tuesday of each month and be available in person or online (must register or email for the virtual link). Find the registration link in our bio :) If you or someone you know is a money expert who wants to share their knowledge with queer/trans survivors, please reach out!

#survivors #lgbtq #durhamnc #economicjustice #queer #trans

While we do our best to put cash directly into survivors hands, in tandem, we thought it would be awesome to create a body doubling/coworking space where we can support each other in sifting through all the shit that goes into getting financial stable. events.title: 🌈 Survivor Roots Support Group
events.description:
At the Southern Queer Survivor Network, we believe in the power of community-driven healing. A root of survivorship is community, something many Queer and Trans people find themselves without after surviving interpersonal violence. We are committed to creating a space where healing isn’t just about individual recovery—it’s about liberation from the systems that harm us.  SQSN is excited to introduce ~ Survivor Roots ~ an ongoing support group intended to support our community, provide consistency, build & deepen connections among LGBTQ+ survivors of interpersonal violence. This is a space where survivors can reclaim their narratives, strengthen their resilience, and build solidarity with one another. Starting in July 2026, we will meet every 2nd & 4th Thursday. This group is available to anyone who identities as:

 -LGBTQIA+
- a survivor of abuse (intimate partner violence, family violence, or any other kind of relational abuse)
- North Carolina resident

The aim of this support group is to:

- Foster community among survivors
- Cultivate feelings of safety, connection, and validation
- Provide education about signs and cycles of Queer IPV
- Promote healing, and when necessary, provide referral to mental health professionals

Register here: bit.ly/SurvivorRoots

Visit Email advocate@lgbtqcenterofdurham.org with any questions!

events.title: 🌈 Survivor Roots Support Group
events.description:
At the Southern Queer Survivor Network, we believe in the power of community-driven healing. A root of survivorship is community, something many Queer and Trans people find themselves without after surviving interpersonal violence. We are committed to creating a space where healing isn’t just about individual recovery—it’s about liberation from the systems that harm us.  SQSN is excited to introduce ~ Survivor Roots ~ an ongoing support group intended to support our community, provide consistency, build & deepen connections among LGBTQ+ survivors of interpersonal violence. This is a space where survivors can reclaim their narratives, strengthen their resilience, and build solidarity with one another. Starting in July 2026, we will meet every 2nd & 4th Thursday. This group is available to anyone who identities as:

 -LGBTQIA+
- a survivor of abuse (intimate partner violence, family violence, or any other kind of relational abuse)
- North Carolina resident

The aim of this support group is to:

- Foster community among survivors
- Cultivate feelings of safety, connection, and validation
- Provide education about signs and cycles of Queer IPV
- Promote healing, and when necessary, provide referral to mental health professionals

Register here: bit.ly/SurvivorRoots

Visit Email advocate@lgbtqcenterofdurham.org with any questions!

events.title: 🤝 Queer Clothing Swap: Back to School Edition
events.description:
Queer Clothing Swap: Back to School Edition🚌

Whether you last sat in a classroom 20 years ago or yesterday, it’s time to school us all on your savvy sustainable fashion skills! This size- and gender-inclusive swap is all about welcoming autumn with community connection, sustainable style, and queer joy.

How It Works✨
Bring your gently used, clean clothing to drop off between 7:00-8:00 PM (please only bring items during this time to keep things organized!).
Starting at 8:00 PM, you’ll be able to “shop” the shared collection and take home pieces that make you feel amazing.
Any unclaimed items will be donated to the LGBTQ Center of Durham’s Trans and GNC closet.

events.title: 🤝 Free Beer Tomorrow (Film Screening)
events.description:
Hi folks, we have some super exciting news to share! Out South Film Festival starts next Thursday at the Carolina Theatre, and Arcana is the proud sponsor of a film called 'Free Beer Tomorrow'. The film will be screening Thursday August 13th at 7:20 at Fletcher Hall. Get your tickets in advance! We're hosting an after party/discussion at Arcana that night, and you know we're also always a good place to meet up before a film, too.

I had the pleasure of screening this documentary in advance- it is SO good, y'all, and so important that we stay connected to a sense of our past and the third places that came before us, offering a safe space to gather, flirt, connect, dance, celebrate, and create a chosen family. And I also super appreciate representation of inter-generational lesbian love and community.

Here's a description of the film:

"An entertaining documentary film project that tells the story of Jacks/Summit’s Station, Ohio’s longest running lesbian owned and operated bar. With interviews from Peter Brown – a classically trained musician turned bar owner – to Rhona R. Rivera, a pioneering LGBTQ+ lawyer & legal scholar, and formers patrons – tap dancers, women’s football players, feminist activists, and drag kings, this engrossing film explores lesbian culture where bars were one of the few safe-havens from an oppressive and homophobic world."

You can find more info here, as well as tickets:
https://carolinatheatre.org/events/film/fee-beer-tomorrow/

this week🌞

our perfect baby angel bookshopbitch’s last day is this wednesday 🥲 we are SO excited for their move to Minneapolis but we are going to miss that gorgeous head of hair and big beautiful smile! come on in, tip them big, and shower them in love!!! how lucky we’ve been to love you all these years!!

events.title: 🤝 DnD Night
events.description:
We have such a full week coming up! DnD on Tuesday, and a quiet night for introverts on Wednesday just before a weekend bursting with music!

Thursday is our first ever queer jazz night, and we’re so excited! Come out and jam, or just listen. The event is free, with a $5-$10 suggested donation (we love our queer musicians)

Friday our most beloved Lee Jean Jr returns for an incredible night of live music! Remember how Lee brought in NYE with a gorgeous rendition of Purple Rain? It’s been getting us through!

Then great beats on Saturday with bardo_bloom  and poetic.note 

Then more jazz on Sunday with the Collective Moment! Come hang, listen, drink, chat, and feel the music 🎶

events.title: 🤝 Courtney Ariel Bowden and Ben Rauscher
events.description:
tonight! Courtney Ariel Bowden is a Durham-based singer-songwriter. Her original music can be found on streaming platforms. An enthusiastic watcher of birds and lover of trees, community, and porch-sitting in North Carolina, Courtney holds the swaying palms, the lull and roar of the pacific ocean at her core, always.

Ben Rauscher is a Durham singer-songwriter who will be performing alongside Courtney tonight (7/19) at 8!!

events.title: 🤝 Queer Craft Night with Shelley
events.description:
new moon in cancer this week, how are we feeling? 

need a shoulder to cry on? need to drown your sorrows in an ice cold cocktail or zero abv bev?
we got you✨

here’s what we have in store this week🌈
tuesday! Queer Craft Night with our cancerian friend, Shelley!! 🦀❤️ she’ll be here to help you write love letters to your bae(s)!! 

wednesday! erinswildmushroom will be leading a special tarot edition of the mycelium meet-up!! 🍄‍🟫🍄

thursday! Hypnagogia w/ Poetic Note🖤

friday! Ally J and Kevin Clark; if you’re looking for an easy, chill friday night then look no further!✨

saturday! Les Trios Chats🎷 live jazz trio!! 

sunday! Courtney Ariel and Ben Rauscher! some good live music to close the week out🎶

events.title: 🤝 Mushroom Meet Up: Tarot Card Edition
events.description:
Hi mushroom fans! We have another mushroom meet up coming up in a week, and this one is a special tarot card edition. Erin is going to be bringing in all of her mushroom tarot decks that you can take a look at. And Rene, one of our amazing tarot card readers, will be available to offer readings from a mushroom tarot deck. Midnight Magic is one of your favorite decks to read from! 

And hopefully, with all this rain we're getting, we can start to talk about what we're finding in the woods, or what we *will* be finding soon. 

The mushroom meet up is open to everyone! Bring your questions and your curiosity and your willingness to learn. We always have a good time!

events.title: 🤝 Live Double Cello Performance by Inference
events.description:
this week!!!! 

we’re closing out pride and welcoming in July! thank you for another incredible pride month, we can’t wait to do it all over again for Durham Pride in September!!! 🤩🏳️‍🌈🏳️‍⚧️💋✨🤩

tomorrow we have a live double cello performance by Inference 🎻🎻✨

the triangleareapaganalliance meet up on Wednesday is for anyone looking to meet and get involved in the local Pagan community! 🌈🩷

Valissa/Okivia Cirilla (formerly Steely Trans) is here on Thursday with some excellent live music! 🪩

Live Jazz trio on Friday featuring our old friends, the Daniel Delorenzo Trio! 🎼🎶

Closed on Saturday for a much needed Saturday off! 💋💤

And Prickly Pair closes out the week with us on Sunday! 🌜

events.title: 🤝 Skaði: Ambient Underground Beats
events.description:
It’s Pride Month, and Arcana has a confession to make- we’re crazy in love with our neighbors at Rubies.✨🏳️‍🌈🏳️‍⚧️

Love between bars is wildly underreported and underappreciated it, so we’re making it public! 💋

This Saturday, when we are basking in the glow of some delicious live jazz from Trio Factual, we still might be secretly (not so secretly) wondering what Fifi Hifi is up to at Adulting.. Or maybe we’re thinking about the song we might sing to impress our beloved Sky at karaoke on Sunday. 🥂

It’s confusing to us sometimes to be a lesbian bar, and pine SO so hard for Bruce. 🥹 We can’t tell you how many times we’ve locked up our doors at midnight and gone racing up the stairs to Rubies for a nightcap, an hour of dancing, and maybe some cute bathroom selfies. 

We love the staff and the vibe and the programming- y’all are just the best neighbors a gay could ever have. The tamales are always hot (but the bartenders are even hotter).

This Friday, for instance! Please please, come out and support Skaði for some ambient underground beats at Arcana on Friday from 9-11pm, THEN spiral up the stairs to Rubies for their Pride party with Sad Muse Club. And mark your calendars, because Sad Muse Club will be back at Arcana on July 16th! If you like Adulting at Rubies, check out the vibe at Arcana on June 20th with Get Out of My Dreams, featuring the one and only Fifi Hifi and Vespertine. 

Can’t wait to see you here, or there, or here AND there 🌈🪩

xoxo Arcana 🐉 😘

events.title: 🌈 TRAMP
events.description:
GAG! is launching a dance party on January 9th! TRAMP was created in response to the community for a dance party — a raw, no disruptions, nonstop music dance party where you can dance freely. Once Bitter Social opened, a new downtown bar by the makers of Bitter Sweet and Johnson Street Yacht Club, it became clear this space was made for just that!

This small intimate space creates a different vibe from any GAG party that promotes getting closer with each other; whether it’s dancing or conversing in one their dark corners.
GAG is bringing two special guest DJs, featuring, Pisces Prince (Gaven Simon) from NYC — featured in So.Gay in 2025 and GHO3 SPINZ from GAG to Death this past Halloween, will pump up the BPMs FOR EVERYONE tramping on the dance floor!

Not only is it a premiere of a new party — but it serves as a birthday celebration of GAG producer, Trey Roberts!

events.title: 🌈 Yard Sale Fundraiser Early Access
events.description:

We are currently accepting donations of household items, toys, clothes, shoes, etc. (no large furniture) at Alliance of Aids Services during their open hours. events.title: 🌈 ASPYRE Youth Leadership Camp
events.description:
Only ✨58✨ days until this year’s ASPYRE Youth Leadership Camp! Are you excited? We are! Registration is live!

ASPYRE Youth Leadership Camp empowers young members of the LGBTQ+ community and their allies to achieve personal growth through activism and community engagement. Camp ASPYRE provides our youth an opportunity to discover their authentic voices while strengthening their leadership and advocacy skills.. all while connecting with other passionate young people who are also ready to create change.

Open to youth ages 13 to 18 who are currently enrolled in high school.

Registration is now open! 🔗 can be found in our bio!

Questions? Contact aspyre@lgbtcenterofraleigh.com.

events.title: 🤝 The Wiley Fosters: Last Show
events.description:
Today, we’re sharing sad news. After almost seven years, Mystery Brewing Company will be closing its doors at the end of the day on October 31st.
.
.
This has been an incredibly difficult decision. We’ve always been undercapitalized, and it’s been a struggle to operate for some time now. We’ve suffered a string of pretty bad luck over the past couple of years: equipment failures, construction and permitting delays, storm-related outages and losses. The end result is that we can no longer afford to operate.
.
.
Over the course of the next week, we’ll be doing the best we can to celebrate everything we love about Mystery to give it a fond farewell, releasing some favorite old beers that we’ve had kicking around in the back of the cooler, and trying to say goodbye the best way we can. If you get a chance, please come and visit us, say hi, and enjoy a pint, a meal, or a night of music for the last time. The Wiley Fosters – our amazing house band – will be playing our last show at the pub on the evening of October 27th.
.
.
We’re enormously proud of the community that has grown up around Mystery, and we’ll miss being here every day for Hillsborough.
.
.
With one last raised glass,
.
.
Erik Lars Myers
Founder, Brewer, CEO
Mystery Brewing Company

events.title: 🤝 BeerChurch: Palo Santo Marron
events.description: Today’s #BeerChurch is dogfishhead’s Palo Santo Marron (2015). An unfiltered, unfettered, unprecedented brown ale aged in handmade wooden brewing vessels. The caramel and vanilla complexity unique to this beer comes from the exotic Paraguayan Palo Santo wood from which these tanks were crafted. Palo Santo means "holy tree," and its wood has been used in South American wine-making communities. This highly roasty and malty brown ale clocks in at 12% ABV. Pub is open from 11:30 AM - 10 PM, and The Sunday Show (free) stand up comedy starts at 8 PM! #hillsboroughNC

events.title: 🎵 Collage Club
events.description:
NEXT WEDNESDAY: Join us on August 19th for Collage Club. Instructor joseph_rafferty returns to host with this month's theme being "Spirits."

Collage Club is a monthly community gathering at The Fruit dedicated to higher education through art. In a non-hierarchical setting rooted in Surrealism, we use provided materials to explore visual play, personification, and the subconscious.

Each session begins with a theme and prompts designed to encourage "creating first and thinking later." 

All experience levels are welcome to join this creative laboratory where things that look like things become something else entirely.

Collage Club — Every 3rd Wednesday at The Fruit. 
7pm - 9pm. Come imagine differently.

events.title: 🎵 Future Fest Connect
events.description:
THIS WEEKEND: We proudly welcome futurefestconnect to downtown Durham!

Future Fest Connect is an introductory gaming and technology experience designed for school-aged students, college learners, and early-career individuals interested in exploring opportunities in game development and the broader digital economy. The event leverages the power of gaming to engage young people through a medium they already know and enjoy, using that connection to inspire interest in STEM/STEAM education pathways and future-ready careers.

As emerging technologies continue to evolve industries, Future Fest Connect aims to help prepare attendees for the evolving workforce by providing direct exposure to professionals working in gaming, technology, art, design, storytelling, and interactive media.

This weekend's festivities include keynote appearances from industry trailblazers, an Epic Games Learning Lab, an E-Sports tournament, a tech and game expo, and more. Check out the full two-day schedule and get tickets online.

events.title: 🌈 Chapel Hill Poet Laureate Application Deadline
events.org: Chapel Hill Arts - Small Town Pride
events.description:
New artist call! ✍️ Chapel Hill is searching for its next Poet Laureate!

Our Poet Laureate serves as an ambassador for poetry, fostering connections between all kinds of writers, poets, and creatives to enrich Chapel Hill’s social and civic life. If you love inspiring creativity and building community through poetry, this role might be for you.

Term & compensation:
🔹 2-year appointment: Jan 2027 - Dec 2028
🔹 $6,000 stipend for selected poet
🔹 $200/finalist for proposals & interviews

Typical responsibilities:
🔹 Write poems for special community moments
🔹 Perform at festivals, events, & council meetings
🔹 Create community poetry experiences
🔹 Facilitate workshops or trainings
🔹 Meet regularly with Town staff

Eligibility:
🔹 Poets 18+ with little, some, or substantial work published & active projects in the last 5 years
🔹 A personal or professional connection to Chapel Hill
🔹 Residency in Chapel Hill preferred, but not required

Apply by Monday, September 14 at 5pm

events.title: 🌈 Application Deadline: Chapel Hill Transit Bus Ceiling Artist Call
events.org: Chapel Hill Arts - Small Town Pride
events.description:
New artist call! 📣 We’re looking for Triangle-based artists and artist teams to design original 2D artwork for chtransit bus ceilings.

Selected artists/teams will each create a single final design to be printed three times as adhesive vinyl and installed on three bus ceilings by a Town contractor. Artwork will be on display for at least 12 months. Vector designs are recommended, as the designs will be ~21 feet long.

Swipe ➡️ to see some past bus ceiling designs.

What’s in it for you?

events.title: 🌈 Aeon Schmoock Exhibition
events.org: Chapel Hill Arts - Small Town Pride
events.description:
Step into alternate worlds by artist Aeon Schmoock in his new exhibition at Chapel Hill Public Library.
 
“This is a collection of paper collages glued onto plywood, polyvinyl chloride, or paper,” Aeon says. “They are all made with a similar style of exact cutting, careful and multiple layering, and a bent towards the humorous and absurd.”

events.title: 🌈 Along the riverbank
events.org: Chapel Hill Arts - Small Town Pride
events.location: Town Hall, 405 MLK Jr. Blvd, Chapel Hill, NC
events.description:
Laser-etched photos, cyanotypes, and pencil drawings make up our newest exhibition at Town Hall: “Along the riverbank” by Elizabeth EJ Trefney (ejtref)

The exhibit is centered around North Carolina waterways and golden handwritten text, meant to evoke regrowth and resilience.

“Armenian proverbs from my great grandfather’s letters and other handwritten notes can be reimagined for our world today,” Elizabeth says. “Like pages torn from a diary, these pieces of moral guidance and simple written notes can be used to paint portraits of climate change and resilience, from the Outer Banks to the Haw River.”

Come visit (it’s free!):
🔹 On display until August 12
🔹 405 MLK Jr. Blvd, Chapel Hill, NC
🔹 Hours: Mon-Fri, 8:30am-5pm

events.title: 🌈 Shelter for the Coming Out
events.org: Chapel Hill Arts - Small Town Pride
events.description:
Last chance to see this year's Pride art installation by morrowdowdle and maxdowdle!

"'Shelter for the Coming Out' speaks to the experience of finally coming out about one’s queer identity, whether it is to a friend, family member, or community," Morrow says. "For queer folk, coming out signifies the moment in which we have decided the pain of keeping our identity secret is so great that it becomes worth the risks of revealing that identity to others. My poem, 'I Come Out to My Daughter,' embodies my own experience in this realm."

On display at 140 West Franklin Street through the end of June. Part of Chapel Hill-Carrboro #SmallTownPride.

events.title: 🌈 Exhibition by Sampada Kodagali Agarwal
events.org: Chapel Hill Arts - Small Town Pride
events.description:
Intricate pattern and storytelling collide in our newest exhibition by Sampada Kodagali Agarwal (ansimit.sampada).

“This exhibition brings together the timeless wisdom of Aesop’s Fables and beloved children’s animal stories, reimagined through the intricate visual language of Gond-inspired art,” Sampada says. “Rooted in the indigenous traditions of central India, Gond art is known for its rhythmic lines, detailed patterns, and deep connection to nature and storytelling.”

Come visit (it’s free!):

events.description:
NOW ON SALE! BEAUTY SCHOOL DROPOUT - Mon Nov 9 @ MOTORCO 

GET TIX @ motorcomusic.com/event/beauty-school-dropout

andmoreagainpresents  PRESENTS

Beauty School Dropout is a Los Angeles rock band redefining what a modern rock band can look and feel like. Built independently and proven on the road, Cole Hutzler, Beepus, Bardo and Colton Flurry combine live-wire guitars, electronic production, massive hooks and a sharp cultural edge with a chaotic, swaggering live show.

“We wanted to make rock music feel fun again,” the band says. “When’s the last time you walked into a party and a band was playing? We want to change that.”

Since emerging in 2021, Beauty School Dropout has generated more than 116 million catalog streams, 510,000 monthly Spotify listeners, and 1 million YouTube views, earning support from BBC Radio 1, Billboard, MTV, NME and Kerrang!, while receiving co-signs and collaborations from artists including Mark Hoppus, Pete Wentz, Royal & the Serpent, Jason Aalon Butler and JXDN. Their catalog includes We Made Plans and God Laughed, READY TO EAT, and their debut full-length album WHERE DID ALL THE BUTTERFLIES GO?, produced by Neal Avron.

On stage, Beauty School Dropout has become one of modern rock’s most explosive young live acts. Touring alongside blink-182, MGK, Matchbox Twenty, Stand Atlantic, Maggie Lindemann, Turnstile and JXDN, the band has built a reputation for performances that blur the line between chaos and control while consistently converting digital momentum into real-world demand. Their growing headline business has packed rooms across the country and established BSD as one of the genre’s fastest-rising live bands.

In 2026, Beauty School Dropout enters its biggest chapter yet. Following a major amphitheater tour supporting MGK, appearances at Vans Warped Tour, the launch of the band’s own BSD Circus event in Los Angeles, Ceremony Festival in Nashville, and a 30-date U.S. headline tour, the band continues to build a rapidly expanding global audience while launching a new era of music led by “Madonna.”

events.title: 🎵 MELTT with Los Eclipses
events.description:
MELTT - Tue Sep 1 @ MOTORCO

GET TIX @ motorcomusic.com/event/meltt/

with LOS ECLIPSES

andmoreagainpresents 

Meltt’s upcoming third album is the culmination of everything the Vancouver indie-pop quartet have accomplished so far, all the while pushing their sound in new and exciting directions. True to its title, Pathways finds Chris Smith [lead vocals, guitar, bass, keys], Jamie Turner [drums, percussion], James Porter [guitar, keys, bass, vocals], and Ian Winkler [bass, keys, guitar] at multiple forks in the road and deciding to take all of them, submerging their sound in new rippling textures while still retaining the warm, textured glow that their music’s contained since their debut EP Visions in 2017. 

Thematically, Pathways approaches what Winkler refers to as “four men approaching their 30s and figuring out their paths and lives.” Big topics abound, from relationships and the aftermath of loss to the strange and uneasy feeling that accompanies navigating the modern world at large. “Our tone is usually pretty optimistic and hopeful, but this time we let some darkness in,” Porter says. “There are so many things we experience individually, but when we get in the studio, it’s clear that we’re on a journey together.”

Whether you’ve been with them since the beginning or are joining them at this very juncture, Pathways will make you thankful that you’re along for the journey.

Ever since Sean Bonnette and Ben Gallaty formed AJJ back in 2004, it’s felt like the world has been playing catch-up. That’s because the band—completed these days by guitarist/keyboard player Preston Bryant, cellist Mark Glick and (relatively) new drummer Kevin Higuchi—has always woven apocalyptic themes and imagery into many of its songs and lyrics. They even self-released a record called Good Luck Everybody in January 2020, as if they knew what was coming. Now though, in 2023, with their eighth studio record and debut on Hopeless Records, Disposable Everything, it feels like the world is finally aligned with AJJ’s doom-laden prophecies – albeit one that still shimmers with hope.

andmoreagainpresents Presents

Madre Cumbia portrait by amandakazemiart

MADRE CUMBIA — a historic collaboration between Los Gaiteros de San Jacinto, Fruko, and Carmelo Torres. More than an album, Madre Cumbia brings together the living roots of Colombian cumbia with the artists who have carried, transformed, and preserved its legacy across generations. From the ancestral sounds of the gaitas and drums to the accordion of the sabanas and the electric bass that helped redefine tropical music, this record celebrates the full arc of cumbia's evolution.

Together, these artists embody nearly every chapter of cumbia's recorded history—from its ceremonial Afro-Indigenous origins and rural accordion traditions to its electrification, international expansion, and enduring legacy. Madre Cumbia is more than a collaboration; it is a gathering of the musicians who have preserved, transformed, and carried one of Latin America's most important musical traditions across generations.

events.title: 🎵 Gyedu Blay Ambolley
events.description:
NOW ON SALE! GYEDU-BLAY AMBOLLEY - Fri Sep 25 @ MOTORCO

GET TIX @ motorcomusic.com/event/gyedu-blay-ambolley

andmoreagainpresents 

Gyedu Blay Ambolley is a musical luminary hailing from Ghana, West Africa, with a staggering 29 albums under his belt. Known affectionately as the "Simigwa Do Man,” Ambolley’s musical journey began in the vibrant port city of Sekondi-Takoradi, in the Western Region of Ghana. His early fascination with music blossomed into a lifelong passion. From mastering his father’s flute at the tender age of eight, to honing his guitar skills under the mentorship of “Uncle Bonku”, Sammy Lartey and Ebo Taylor, Ambolley’s musical odyssey has been nothing short of extraordinary.  This all led to Ambolley becoming a musical life force and exploding on the scene in 1973 with a jazzy highlife sound called 'SIMIGWA-DO'. His name has become synonymous with Simigwa music and dance.

Coming of age amidst the zenith of Ghana’s highlife era, Ambolley emerged as a pivotal figure in its evolution, lending his talents to esteemed bands such as Houghas Extraordinaires, Meridians Of Tema and Ghana Broadcasting Band. It was during this time that he caught the attention of his compatriot and friend, Ebo Taylor, who recruited Ambolley to be a member of the Uhuru Dance Band. This all lead to a transformative journey to Nigeria in 1973, where they shared the stage with the legendary Fela Kuti at his renowned Shrine venue. 

Ambolley not only embraces his musical roots but also pioneers the fusion of Ghanaian highlife with soul and funk influences from across the Atlantic. With Simigwa, Ambolley seized the opportunity to showcase his own musical prowess and embark on a journey of experimentation. A main inspiration for this album was the work of the mighty Mr. James Brown, something that is evident from the rhythm section, horns, vocal stabs and percussion breaks throughout the record.
